title: Street vendors' horns and music everywhere in New Orleans
summary: The bottle man, waffle man and comb-blowers, and girls dancing on the corner by parade bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I used to hear a lot of music around the streets, you know, vendors and people selling things. Did they all sing or play or anything?
You know, like when the Bishop man went by or somebody, did they sing songs in the streets, you know, the cars and so on?

Yeah, the bottle man used to have one of them tin horns he used to blow and try to play all the stuff the bands to play. Oh yeah? Like the bottles and junk and all that. Toot. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. The waffle man used to go around he had a bugle. Uh-huh. Yeah. What did he play on it? He tried to play something. He used to play. That guy, that waffle man, he done something. He made some kind of big record. He played something on that thing and got in the money. Oh yeah?
You ever heard of it? We're talking about this guy recently you mean? You were aware of the Google? Yeah. Yeah. Sure. Bugle in sand. Something.
Did you see him in the audience? Uh-huh.
Guy used to take combs, you know, and take a piece of paper and blow a comb. Walking them down the street, everybody's been just blowing on that comb.

Entertaining himself, yeah. He was listening with the bands playing each week playing it, you know. But there was a lot of girls hanging around jazz musicians. Oh man, when we'd be advertising, they'd have more sideline. All the girls walking, you know, dancing out on the corner. She'd stop and be out there dancing on the corner. Hold on. Oh, this would come around them. Yeah, they'd dance. You couldn't stop them. Must have been music everywhere.
